_doc: Which defined tapped holes each neck / head printed connector uses (same format as robot/body/fastening/connector_screws.json, kept next to the neck / head builders because the neck parts have no side prefix). connector: manifest name of the printed part; sides: side prefixes it exists on (default R_ and L_; the empty prefix here); clamped: the parts the screw head presses on (their outer face along the hole axis ends the stack); groups: standard_part = manifest instance holding the holes (an XM335 case or horn registered to robot/actuators/interfaces/standard-parts.json), holes = hole labels of that definition in screw order, name = screw part name in the manifest ({i} = index in holes; the legacy names stay so part settings and the assembly order keep resolving: the generated thread / length are in the part's screw_plan), owning_link = link the screw rides with, head = standard of the head (robot/body/checks/data/hardware.json screw_standards). Where the clamped part's contact face lies relative to a hole opening is measured from the standard part's mesh (defined_holes.py), never typed.
